chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Four (types of people) for whom a supplication is not answered: A man who sits in his house saying, 'O Allah, grant me sustenance,' so it is said to him, 'Did I not command you to seek (it)?' And a man who has a wife, so he supplicates against her, so it is said to him, 'Did I not make her matter to you?'
And a man who had wealth, so he squandered it, so he says, 'O Allah, grant me sustenance,' so it is said to him, 'Did I not command you with moderation? Did I not command you with rectitude?'
Then He said, 'And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy, and are between that, standing firm (in balance).'
And a man who had wealth, so he lent it out without clear evidence, so it is said to him, 'Did I not command you with witnessing?'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Imran ibn Abu Aasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — similar to it.
ai.seo_question: Why is a person's supplication rejected despite their devotion?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the principle that divine acceptance of du'a is contingent upon human agency and ethical consistency, specifically linking the supplicant's actions to the specific request. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'preparation of the vessel' for divine grace, noting that laziness, marital discord, financial squandering, or procedural negligence in transactions act as barriers to answered prayers. The reference to 'those who spend not extravagantly nor stingily' connects this practical wisdom to the Quranic ideal of balanced living.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah Bin Ibrahim, from Ja’far Bin Ibrahim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Four (people), a supplication for not be Answered for them – a man who sits in his house saying, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>!

Grace me sustenance’. So He<sup>azwj</sup> would Say to him: “Did I<sup>azwj</sup> not Command you with the seeking (of the livelihood)?” and a man who has a wife for him, so he supplicates against her, so He<sup>azwj</sup> would Say to him: “Did I<sup>azwj</sup> not Make her matter to you?”.

And a man who had wealth for him, so he spoilt it, so He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Say to him: ‘Grace me sustenance’. So He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Say to him: “Did I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> not Command you with the moderation? Did I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> not Command you with the righteousness?”.

Then Heazwj Says [25:67] And they who when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy, and between that by stature”; and a man who did have wealth for him, but he lent it without any evidence, so Heazwj would Say to him: “Did Iazwj not Command you with the witnessing?’

Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Imran Bin Abu Aasim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> – similar to it.
en.sarwar: 2. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from ibn Faddal from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim from Ja’far ibn Ibrahim from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The prayers of four kinds of people are not heard: a man who sits home and says, ‘O Lord, grant me sustenance,’ and it is said to him, “Have I not commanded you to work?” a man who is troubled by his wife so he prays for relief, but he will be asked, ‘Have 1 not made dissolving marriage lawful?’
A man who has destroyed his wealth and asks, ‘O Lord, grant me wealth,’ he will be asked, “Have I not commanded you to spend it moderately and have I not commanded you to make corrections?”
Then the Imam read from the Holy Quran, ‘. . . who in their spending are neither extravagant nor stingy but maintain moderation,’ [25:67]
and a man who lends money to others without witnesses as evidence and it is said to him, ‘Have I not commanded you to ask for witnesses as testimony?”’
Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from ‘Umar ibn abu ‘Asim from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) a similar Hadith.
